subject: Observability & eval onboarding — proposed roadmap and next steps
summary: Post-call recap for Finlytics discovery: confirmed observability gaps (spiky p95 latency, cost attribution gaps, no golden prompts), defined success criteria and short-term eval playbook; agreed technical follow-up with solutions engineer and deliverables (dashboard spec, tracing hook doc, golden prompt set).
messages:
From: Ava Lytton <ava.lytton@finlytics.co>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intro: Observability & eval needs — Finlytics x Redwood

Marcus / team — thanks again for the intro call earlier. Quick recap from our side and the things we'd like to prioritize as we evaluate Redwood: 

Pain points we described:
- Latency spikes on large-batch inference (p95 occasionally >1.6s) impacting UX during peak spread trades.
- Model updates have introduced subtle QA regressions (we only catch these manually today).
- Cost attribution is opaque — we need token-level cost per route and per-user grouping.
- No current "golden prompt" suite for regression checks; hard to validate behavioral parity across model variants.

Success criteria for pilots (high level):
1) Stable p95 <= 800ms on our baseline prompt mix at 90% traffic.
2) Auto-detected regression alerts (precision-focused) within 24h of a rollout.
3) Dashboard + traces that let our SREs triage model-induced latency vs infra-induced latency.
4) A reproducible golden prompt set and eval harness we can run nightly.

Asks / next steps we discussed:
- A short spec for the dashboards & KPIs (p50/p95/p99, token cost, error rates).
- Example tracing hooks you recommend (span names, where to place traces from our middleware).
- An example golden prompt JSON structure and how Redwood ties eval results to rollout guardrails.
- Timeline: we'd like a technical deep-dive next week (Dev on our side will join).

Attaching our telemetry requirements spreadsheet for reference (FNL-telemetry-reqs.xlsx).

Thanks — happy to iterate on the list.

— Ava
Ava Lytton
Director of Product Engineering | Finlytics
ava.lytton@finlytics.co

Ava — great meeting, and thanks for the clear requests. Short recap from our side plus proposed next steps so we have shared expectations.

Key takeaways (condensed):
- Spike mitigation and visibility are top priority (p95 target ~800ms).
- Nightly evals with a golden prompt set to gate rollouts are required.
- Token-level cost attribution and per-route dashboards needed for product + finance.

What we'll deliver before the technical deep-dive:
1) Redwood eval onboarding checklist (attached) — what we need from you and what we provide.
2) Dashboard spec draft (p50/p95/p99, cost by route, error types, user cohort breakdown).
3) Tracing hooks primer — recommended span names and where to instrument the call chain.
4) Example golden-prompts-sample.json and a short runbook for nightly regression alerts.

Proposed schedule:
- Tomorrow EOD: upload dashboard spec + checklist to shared Drive.
- Tue 2027-06-15 10:00am PT: technical deep-dive (Dev on your side + Priyom as Solutions Engineer).

If that works, I'll calendar the deep-dive and Priyom will prepare the tracing examples and a small demo showing our regression alert flow.

One note on rollouts: our standard recommendation is canary + eval gate (nightly), with auto-fallback on guardrail violations; happy to tailor the sensitivity to Finlytics' risk tolerance.

Thanks again — looking forward to the next call.

— Marcus Lin

Ava / Marcus — adding technical detail ahead of the deep-dive. Attaching a compact set of examples and a minimal instrumentation guide.

Tracing hooks (recommended):
- Outbound inference span: redwood.inference.request (tags: model_id, seq_len, route, user_cohort)
- Tokenization span: redwood.inference.tokenize (tags: tokenizer, input_tokens)
- Backend GPU queue span: redwood.runtime.queue (tags: gpu_id, batch_size)
- Each span should carry a request_id and parent_request_id to correlate across services.

Dashboard KPIs (required fields):
- p50/p95/p99 latency (service + model split)
- Token cost per request & tokens/sec by route
- Model regression score delta (nightly baseline vs candidate)
- Errors by class (timeout, decode_error, infra_error)

Golden prompt format (sample):
- JSON array where each entry: {"id": "gp-001", "prompt": "...", "expected_behavior": "classification: high/medium/low", "metrics": {"exact_match": true, "embedding_similarity": 0.95}}

Rollout guardrails we propose for Finlytics pilot:
1) Canary at 10% for 12 hours with continuous evaluation on golden prompts.
2) If nightly regression delta > 2% for precision or if p95 increases > 15% vs baseline, auto-fallback to previous variant and pager notification.
3) Optional: soft-alerting window for low-severity deltas to avoid noisy rollbacks while we tune sensitivity.

Attachments in this email: golden-prompts-sample.json (example entries), redwood-trace-primer.md (span naming + examples). I'll upload both to the Drive link Marcus will create.

Looking forward to the deep-dive.

— Priyom
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
